applies_why: The rule governs a judge-seat collision where the pressed witnesses are the pressing side's own chain read together, and this text decides such a chain-against-chain dispute.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse" — one reading allows an underdetermined chain-vs-chain outcome when neither side's chain forces the other, without demanding a single contrary stating verse; the other would require explicit footing-by-footing resolution.
why: The judge resolved the Acts 2:30 collision by comparing the parties' chains and finding neither forced the other, rather than requiring a single contrary verse.
